question: After the degenerate selector pilot: is acceptance blocked by proposal quality or by the gate/panel? Replay the archived known-good skill edit (alfworld-flash attempt 4, the only edit that ever passed this gate) through a scripted proposer on the same 8/8 config, removing proposal quality from the equation.

design.workspace: fresh ALFWorld skills workspace, --train 8 --validation 8, flash, thinking disabled, max_steps 1
design.proposer: scripted emitter writes the archived attempt4-proposal.diff verbatim (zero model calls for proposing)
design.panels: frozen 6-seen + 6-unseen test panel identical to all prior studies

validation.per_task: identical outcome vector to the parent re-measure - zero wins, zero losses

diagnosis: VALIDATION REPRESENTATIVENESS IS THE BINDING CONSTRAINT. The known-good edit - worth +2 games over both controls on the frozen test panel - was invisible on this validation draw: same mean (0.875) AND the same per-task outcome vector as the parent (train-split games, all solved identically). No mean-based or paired-task gate arithmetic could have accepted it, because the 8 train-split validation games carried no signal on this draw. The original 2026-10-12 acceptance was a lucky validation draw; the 2026-10-19 pilot nulls were unlucky draws of the same coin. Gate-ability at this design is noise-limited and split-limited, not quality-limited.
implications: validation panels must be drawn from the same distribution as the test panels (seen/unseen layouts), not from leftover train-split games - a pack design change, not a gate mechanism change
a paired per-task gate was considered and rejected for now: on this real draw it would also have rejected (zero task flips), and the deeper fix is representative validation
the earlier selector-pilot verdict stands with a sharper cause: acceptance was impossible on that validation draw regardless of gate strictness
audit: zero expected-answer leakage, zero silent bypass; verify lineage ok
limits: One replay draw, one seed, one archived edit. The diagnosis is about this pack design (train-split validation) at this panel size; other packs (BBH, HumanEval) evaluate their actual test distribution and are unaffected.

recheck_2026_10_21.question: Does representative validation (4 seen + 4 unseen, disjoint from test) make the archived edit gateable?

validation.per_task: identical outcome vectors again - zero wins, zero losses

final_panel.note: this draw the baseline condition also saturated 12/12, so the edit showed no test-panel advantage either

recheck_2026_10_21.conclusion: Representative validation is necessary but not sufficient: across three replays the edit's effect is small and draw-dependent on every panel. Single-draw gate-ability at 8 games is a lottery regardless of validation source. The empirically demonstrated acceptance path is persistence: the original study accepted on attempt 4 of 4 after three failures - each attempt is a fresh draw. Pilots ran 1-2 attempts and saw nothing. Implication for study design: attempts >= 4 for small-effect edits, or larger panels; both cost budget by the (1+attempts)*(train+2*validation) rule.
